transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-11
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Chopra (Redwood SE), Evan Holt (CSM), Marta Ruiz (Head of ML, AstraNova), Devon Lee (Platform), Samir Patel (Product), Lian Zhao (Security)

Summary:
Quick QBR-styled checkin focusing on a recent usage spike, unit cost creep, reliability blips during peak, and aligning on a pilot scope + budget guardrails. Action items and a next checkpoint scheduled.

Topics: usage trends, cost drivers (token distribution + seq length), dedicated vs hosted routing, batching and quantization options, security and KMS, pilot sizing and SLA expectations.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 50 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Marta: Marta here, hi.
[00:06] Devon: Devon here.
[00:08] Samir: Samir, hi.
[00:10] Lian: Lian from security.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. Evan and Priya from our side as well. Main agenda - review the spike you saw last week, cost drift, and then workshop some guardrail options for the next quarter.
[00:30] Marta: Yeah thanks. The spike was odd — we saw a 3x increase for a six hour window. It coincided with a marketing push but the latencies also went up and we had a couple of timed-out requests that affected the user flow.
[00:45] Priya: Can you share the approximate token distribution for that period? Was it longer sequences or lots of short chat calls?
[00:52] Devon: Mostly long. Our FAQ flow pushed to long-form answers, average sequence jumped from 120 to ~560 tokens during the window.
[01:10] Samir: Also some unexpected reruns due to front-end retries, we think the client retried at 3xx errors which multiplied calls.
[01:22] Jordan: Classic retry amplification. Ok so cost drivers are twofold: longer sequences and retry storms. For guardrails we usually recommend three levers: front-end retry limits + backoff, prefix caching and KV reuse, and batching/quantization to reduce per-token cost.
[01:40] Marta: Curious on batching — we are worried batching will increase tail latency for interactive flows.
[01:48] Priya: Right, batching is a trade. Our runtime supports adaptive continuous batching - it will only batch short requests together and has latency SLO knobs. We can simulate your traffic mix to show expected p50/p95 impact.
[02:05] Devon: Where does dedicated fit? If we move to a dedicated pool, does that solve the occasional timeout?
[02:12] Priya: Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and less noisy neighbors, but doesn't remove app-level retries. It helps latency stability and throughput headroom; coupling with autoscale policies we can absorb spikes.
[02:28] Lian: From security side we need to confirm KMS policies and whether the audit logs keep token-level redaction. Also need to know if private deployment is an option — some of our PHI-adjacent logs may need to stay in our VPC.
[02:45] Jordan: We have private deployment options and KMS/HSM integration; we'll provide the security pack. For audit logging we can provide anonymized token-level metrics and full request traces when allowed.
[03:00] Marta: Another ask — can you run a bench of our 512 token workload on both hosted and a dedicated small pool so we can see the unit economics?
[03:10] Priya: Absolutely. We'll run a two-hour window sim using your sample prompts. Helps us show batching gains and quantization tradeoffs.
[03:20] Samir: On pricing we need a guardrail that keeps monthly spend within a predictable band — say +/- 15% — otherwise finance objects.
[03:27] Jordan: For pilots we usually propose a three-tier sizing: baseline (hosted, auto), reserve (dedicated small pool with burst), and committed (dedicated with monthly reservation). We'll model 3 scenarios and show expected unit cost and headroom.
[03:45] Devon: How quick can you turn around recommendations? We want to present to finance next week.
[03:50] Jordan: We'll send a costing model and recommendations by Friday 2025-03-14.
[03:58] Priya: Quick note on quantization — for your workload (long sequences) we recommend a mixed strategy: 8-bit for repeats/prefix, 4-bit for hot-path scoring if accuracy allows. We'll include quality vs cost estimates.
[04:15] Marta: Any tradeoffs on latency with 4-bit?
[04:18] Priya: Slightly higher compute variance but overall lower token cost; we'll show measured p95 differences in the bench.
[04:30] Evan: I want to flag the operational side — last week's incident didn't have a clear rollback. We recommend a simple fallback policy to a smaller model family to keep the flow live while we remediate.
[04:40] Devon: That would be helpful, our front-end can switch model endpoints if you provide an A/B style routing rule.
[04:46] Jordan: We'll propose a fallback policy in the playbook. Also Evan will add incident traces and a rollback checklist to the shared space.
[04:56] Lian: On compliance: we need SLA language around data retention and support for customer-managed keys. Can you pull sample contract language?
[05:05] Jordan: Yes, we'll include a sample clause and the SOC2 summary.
[05:12] Samir: For the pilot, what's the expected timeline from our side?
[05:15] Jordan: If we get sample traffic and confirm KMS constraints, we can schedule bench next week and have a pilot terms sheet within seven business days.
[05:25] Marta: Sounds good. One more — can you show us a cost forecast that accounts for both marketing-driven spikes and normal usage? We need to see worst-case monthly spend for finance.
[05:36] Priya: We'll include a stress scenario with headroom planning: the recommended reserved capacity plus autoscale buffer to keep spend within the guardrail.
[05:45] Devon: On the technical checklist — I'll send the sample prompts and config for tokenization and pre/post processing.
[05:52] Jordan: Great, we'll wrap with next steps and owners. Any final questions?
[05:58] Marta: No, thanks. This helped clarify.
[06:00] Jordan: Thanks team, we'll follow up with the model and bench scheduling and the costing scenarios.

Recap / Commitments:
- Redwood to run a 2-hour benchmark for AstraNova's 512-token distribution on hosted + dedicated configurations (Priya)
- Jordan to send a three-tier costing model and pilot commercial terms (Jordan)
- Devon to provide sample traffic and prompt corpus (Devon)
- Security exchange: SOC2 and KMS requirements (Lian & Redwood security)
- Follow-up checkpoint scheduled for 2025-03-21 (30 minutes)

Notes on transcript fidelity: occasional mis-attribution and minor transcription errors (names and acronyms may be slightly off).
